sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: This lesson is about rules and advice: what is required, what you need to do, what is a good idea, what is not allowed, and what is not necessary. The key point: mustn't and don't have to mean very different things.

examples.en: I have to read the contract.
examples.translation: I need to, because of the situation

examples.en: I don't have to buy supplies.

blocks.text: must + the action as in the dictionary means it is required: You must take your belongings. must is the same for everyone, has no -s, and never has to after it.

examples.en: We must check the expiry date.

fixes.wrong: You must to take your belongings.

drill.why: After must: the action as in the dictionary, no -s, no to.

blocks.text: have to + action means you need to, often because of the situation: I have to read the contract. With he / she use has to. Without to the meaning changes: I have read means it is already done.

formula.text: I / you / we / they: have to + action

examples.en: I have to read the contract.
She has to enter her occupation.
examples.translation: the form asks for her job

examples.en: I occasionally have to work late.
He has to follow the diversion.
I have to show proof of purchase.
examples.translation: the shop asks for the receipt

fixes.wrong: I has to read the contract.
fixes.right: I have to read the contract.

fixes.wrong: She have to enter her occupation.
fixes.right: She has to enter her occupation.

blocks.text: should + action is advice: it is a good idea. You should consult a teacher. should also has no -s and no to.

examples.en: We should use up the milk.
examples.translation: finish it before it goes bad

fixes.wrong: You should to consult a teacher.

blocks.text: ought to is also advice, almost like should, but with to: You ought to set a budget. Here to is needed, and there is no -s.

examples.en: You ought to set a budget.
We ought to find the cause.
You ought to keep in mind the departure time.
We ought to express our gratitude.

fixes.wrong: You ought read the national news.
fixes.right: You ought to read the national news.

fixes.wrong: You oughts to read the national news.
fixes.right: You ought to read the national news.

drill.why: ought always needs to, unlike should and must.

blocks.text: mustn't means it is not allowed: You mustn't ignore the rules. It is a strong no. Do not use it for “not necessary” — that is don't have to. No to after mustn't.

fixes.wrong: You mustn't to ignore the rules.

sections.title: don't have to and needn't — not necessary

blocks.text: Not necessary, you can choose: don't / doesn't have to or needn't. I don't have to buy supplies; You needn't reply straight away. This is not a rule against it — that is mustn't. No to after needn't; to after don't have.

formula.text: not necessary: don't / doesn't have to + action

examples.en: I don't have to buy supplies.
She doesn't have to bring a photocopy.
He doesn't have to head back yet.

fixes.wrong: She don't have to bring a photocopy.
fixes.right: She doesn't have to bring a photocopy.

fixes.wrong: I don't has to buy supplies.
fixes.right: I don't have to buy supplies.

fixes.wrong: You needn't to collect it personally.

drill.question: At the art class the organiser gives out the paints. Buying them is not needed, but it is not forbidden either. What do you say?
drill.optionB: I don't have to buy supplies.
drill.explain: Not necessary: don't have to. mustn't means not allowed.

blocks.text: The polite request from lesson 19 also appears here: Could I pay separately? Could first, then I and the action with no to.

examples.en: Could I send it by post?

drill.prompt: Ask politely if you can try it.

fixes.wrong: You must to take your belongings.
I has to read the contract.
fixes.right: I have to read the contract.

fixes.wrong: You ought read the national news.
fixes.right: You ought to read the national news.

fixes.wrong: You needn't to collect it personally.

blocks.text: to appears only in have to and ought to. After must, should, mustn't and needn't the action comes straight away. Not allowed — mustn't; not necessary — don't have to or needn't.
Required — must. Needed because of the situation — have / has to. Advice — should or ought to. Not allowed — mustn't. Not necessary — don't have to or needn't.

examples.en: We must go through the list.
He should stand up for his friend.
